To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Tau-B is a robust and useful measure for the component analysis of Likert scale data.
the Pearson correlation and Kendall Tau-B are the most robust measures of association for use with Likert scale attititudinal data, with large or with small samples.
Tau-B and the Pearson r are the most robust coefficients for analyzing Likert scale data and the tetrachoric, Phi, and Phi/PhiMax coefficients are less robust.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the use of the incomplete principal components method for the analysis of Likert scale data and the selection of a coefficient of association that will be most robust with respect to the type of data and the sample size.

the development of a new measure of association, the Kendall Tau-B coefficient, which is based on a simple and easily computed formula, and which has been shown to be robust and useful for the component analysis of attitudinal data based on a Likert scale.
the use of the incomplete principal components method to reduce the dimensionality of a set of variables and to identify the underlying dimensions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of Tau-B as a measure of association for the component analysis of Likert scale data would seem most appropriate, and that the Pearson r is the next most appropriate measure.
the Pearson r and the Tau-B are the most appropriate measures to use for the incomplete principal component analysis of Likert scale data.
the Pearson r and Tau-B coefficients are most robust for the component analysis of simulated Likerts scale data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, with the exception of the measures based on 4 x 4 tables (Pearson r and Tau-B), all measures of association were affected by the type of departure from normality, and the magnitude of the distortion.

the use of Pearson’s product moment coefficient of correlation, tetrachoric r, Phi, Phi/Phi max, and Tau-B coefficients for the component analysis of simulated attitudinal data based on a known underlying factor pattern, and possessing different types and severities of distributional distortion, is not recommended.
the Pearson r and Tau-B coefficients should be used for the principal components analysis of attitudinal data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Pearson r and Tau-B coefficients should be considered when performing the component analysis of Likert scale data and the coefficients based on 2x2 tables should not be used.
the incomplete principal component analysis of Likert scale data can be conducted with the Pearson r, t, and Tau-B coefficients, and that the latter coefficient is preferred.
the incomplete principal components model is robust and the Pearson correlation and Tau-B are the most robust measures for assessing association between variables.
